items.text: A chart of accounts from your country's template, and a fiscal year that starts in any month.
Posting accounts by role, so every document knows where its entry goes.
Documents post their own journal entries. Refused postings wait in a backlog and retry.
Recurring journals, invoices, bills and standing payments.
Payroll posted to the ledger by department.
Period close with a checklist, revaluation, year end and reopening.
Trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow and ageing, exported as PDF, XLSX or CSV.
Obligations and a cash-flow forecast with three scenarios.
Intercompany links and group consolidation with eliminations.
Consolidated cash flow and a comparative column for the group.
Staged acquisitions and dividends eliminated by themselves.
Budgets that warn or block at the requisition, the order and the invoice.
Payment requests with a maker and a checker, and payment batches.
Expenses, reimbursements, cash advances, mileage and per diem.
A hash-chained audit trail. The person who asks cannot approve their own finance documents.
Bank statement import from CSV, OFX, MT940 or CAMT.053.
Reconciliation sessions that lock when they are approved.
Transfers between your own accounts, cash in transit and exchange differences.
Payments sent through real bank rails, with live checks on each provider.
A speed pass so large ledgers stay quick.

connectsTitle: Connected to the rest of the business

connects.text: Invoices, receipts and credit notes post to the ledger by themselves.
Supplier bills and payments post as they are approved.
Stock movements post at their value, by your costing method.
Each payroll run posts salaries and what is owed on them.
Tax posts to the ledger by tax code.
Wallets are accounts in the books.

faq.q: Do I have to write a journal entry for every sale?
faq.a: No. Invoices, receipts, bills, payroll and stock movements post their own entries. If the books refuse one, it waits in a backlog and is tried again.

faq.q: Can I bring in my bank statements?
faq.a: Yes. Import them as CSV, OFX, MT940 or CAMT.053, then match them in a reconciliation session that locks when it is approved.

faq.q: Can someone approve their own payment?
faq.a: No. The person who asks for a finance document cannot approve it, and every change is kept in the audit trail.
